checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan v0.2: boundary fixtures, structural drift report, JSONL output

impact_assessment.why: Programmers need boundary-value test data and actionable fixture-drift diagnostics, not just a pass/fail byte check
impact_assessment.benefits: Fewer hand-written edge cases; reviewable drift diffs; streaming-friendly fixture format
impact_assessment.risks: contract: JSONL and drift text become public output; dependency: std only; concurrency: single-threaded pure functions; state: new generation mode must not perturb seeded stream
impact_assessment.mitigation: Golden byte tests for all formats, pure deterministic edge generation independent of the seeded stream, ADRs recorded before edits

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan v0.3: fixture diff command and multi-fixture manifest gate

impact_assessment.why: Real projects keep several fixtures; reviewing and gating them one command at a time does not scale
impact_assessment.benefits: One CI command for all fixtures; structural diff of two committed fixtures without regenerating
impact_assessment.risks: contract: manifest format and exit codes are public; dependency: std only; concurrency: sequential entries; state: multi-fixture loop must be an explicit machine
impact_assessment.mitigation: Versioned manifest refused on unknown version, dedicated ManifestRun state machine, golden and CLI tests for both commands

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan v0.4: dogfood the manifest gate in AIKit Phase 4 and add JSON reports

impact_assessment.why: A green AIKit check should also prove the project's committed fixtures, and CI systems need machine-readable results
impact_assessment.benefits: Fixture drift fails the same gate as tests; JSON output enables dashboards and automation
impact_assessment.risks: contract: JSON report schema and gate name are public; dependency: std only; concurrency: sequential; state: report builder must be pure
impact_assessment.mitigation: Versioned JSON schema with golden tests, a pure report module, and a full gate re-run after config change

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan v0.5: seed override and stdin schema input

impact_assessment.why: Scripts need to explore seeds and pipe schemas without creating temporary files
impact_assessment.benefits: A single seed can be overridden on the CLI; schemas can come from stdin; still no state outside the machine
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --seed and '-' path are new inputs; dependency: std only; concurrency: single-threaded; state: seed override must flow through the same machine fields
impact_assessment.mitigation: Golden tests for seed override, stdin integration test, ADR recorded before edits
